summary: Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858 and held a post at Uppsala University. He also taught Sten Konow.
Soshu Nishioka (b. 1948) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.
Soshuku Shibatani (b. 1954) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and held a post as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University, attested in 2015.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She held positions at the University of Houston, the University of North Carolina Wilmington (attested 2020), and Harvard University (~2020–2022).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma (b. 1937) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (~1964–1966, PhD), and was a professor at Aligarh Muslim University (attested 2006–2012).

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earning an M.A. from the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD from Columbia University, where she held a post attested in 2013.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France (~1821–1832). Succeeding Abel-Rémusat in 1832, he served as professor and administrator at the Collège de France until 1873.
Stanley Abe specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts at Duke University (attested in 1995 and 2004) and taught Jungmin Ha.

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia College, the University of Tübingen, and Yale University, where he subsequently held a faculty post from ~1964 to 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard, later holding posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 1973) and Harvard University (~1976–2001) as professor of anthropology.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Harvard (~1958–1962), served as professor at the University of London (~1962–1968), and was later emeritus professor at Yale University (attested 1981–2008).

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania (~1954–1959) and served as distinguished professor emeritus of history at UCLA (~1959–2002).
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Alex Wayman from ~1965 to 1970.

Stefan Baums specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (~2002–2009) and held posts at the University of Copenhagen (2002), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2012), and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2012).

Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stockholm University (PhD awarded by 2009) under Per-Arne Berglie, Erik af Edholm, and David Germano, later holding a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (attested 2012).
Stefan Maul (b. 1958) is a scholar of history/archaeology and linguistics. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin from 1987 to 1995 and at Heidelberg University in 1995.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) and took up a post at SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice. He held posts at Padua, Soka University, the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, Ca' Foscari, and Oxford.

Stella Kramrisch (1896–1993) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919) and held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1923–1950) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1950–1972).

Sten Konow (1867–1948) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist. He studied under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel, and held posts at Oslo, Berlin State Library, Archaeological Survey of India, Hamburg (1914–1919), and Visva-Bharati (1924–1925).
